newsitem.title: GREECE: Banks lead rebound, Greek equities gain 1.07pct.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead rebound, Greek equities gain 1.07pct.

text.p: Greek shares shrugged off Tuesday's sharp losses despite a weak opening and rebounded 1.07 percent as banks were enlivened by renewed buying interest.
Market participants said the market displayed strong underlying support, completing a correction faster than anticipated.
"Wednesday's performance proved that the market has a stronger momentum than was initially thought," said Spyros Bellos, managing director at Kappa Securities.
The correction was shorter than the three-to-four session slump many anticipated following Tuesday's large drop, he added.
The Athens bourse' benchmark index edged 1.07 percent or 17.30 points higher to 1,639.01 from Tuesday's 1,621.71 close.

In early trading, it hit a low at 1,596.67 on weakness in banks and construction, but prices clawed their way back up as the morning wore on and banks shares turned upbeat due to high investor interest.
Banks climbed 1.01 percent with industrials gaining 0.69 percent.

"The swift rebound in prices may well signal that Tuesday's price decline was only a slight hiccup rather than the long-awaited price correction," said Vasilis Kaloudis, fund manager at International Mutual Funds.
Turnover was a heavy 27.0 billion drachmas in volume of 6.5 million shares which included several block trades.
Other brokers would like to see prices consolidating at current levels before the market resumed its climb on fundamentals.

"The rebound is very ominous in a technical sense. I would rather see a consolidation at current levels before the market gathers new strength to move higher again," said broker Nicos Ritsonis, at Beta Securities.
The new leg to the rally should be based on key macroeconomic news, including a restraint in fiscal expenses and easing interest rates, he added.
Money attracted to the equities market from the fixed-income area were not seen returning to their safe haven even if profit taking continued at current levels.
"The downward trend in interest rates inhibits a return of funds from equities to fixed-income as the yield gap has narrowed significantly," said International's Kaloudis.
Foreign institutional investors were expected to have a larger impact on prices in the coming weeks as we approach the second part-flotation and the share capital increase of OTE telecom.
"Foreign portfolios may have to lighten their positions in Greek shares in order to take up more shares of OTE without increasing their overall weighting in Greek equities," said Kaloudis.
There were block trades in ErgoBank and Hellenic Bottling.
Other blocks were done in shares of Commercial Bank, Titan Cement, Aluminium of Attica, Hellenic Biscuit, Alpha Finance, Aspis Pronia, and Metrolife.
Advancing stocks led decliners 133 to 95 with 25 stocks unchanged on 253 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,094-1,124. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, firmed 105 drachmas to 6,505.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted higher at 662.50-704.78. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $89.79-$91.48. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,378-3,598 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $22.01-23.71. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted higher at 272-305 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
